Welcome to the **High Throughput Sequencing data analysis (ChIP-seq)** workshop.

During this course you will learn to:

- Connect to a server
- QC your data
- Align to a reference Genome
- Visualise your data
- Perform Peak Calling
- Examine Motifs
- Explore Regions of Interest

This course is hosted by the Bioinformatics Core at the [DRP-HCB](https://biology.ed.ac.uk/drp).

### Course Setup

## IGV

Today we will be using the **Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV)** to view our alignments etc., this needs to be installed on your own machines

Please find download and installation instructions [here](https://igv.org/doc/desktop/#DownloadPage/).

## Environment
For the command line portion If you are using the DRP-HCB Bioinformatics server for this course then all of the data and software is already installed. If you are working through this course from a different Linux computer or server, please make sure the following tools are installed:

::: resources
<h2><i class="fas fa-save"></i> Required software</h2>

- Fastqc
- Multiqc
- TrimGalore
- Bowtie2
- Samtools
- Macs2
- HOMER
- Deeptools

An easy way to install is through [conda](https://continuumio-docs.readthedocs-hosted.com/miniconda/). Check out [our guide](https://drp-hcb-bioinformatics.github.io/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/software.html) and explore how to install and work with conda. Tools can then be installed by downloading the environment (yml) file and running the following commands to install and activate the environment.

``` bash
wget https://github.com/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/HTS_data_analysis_ChIP-seq/blob/main/htsdac_env.yml

conda env create -f htsdac_env.yml

conda activate htsdac_env
```

:::
